newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA PLANS NEW DRIVING LICENCES FROM 1998.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA PLANS NEW DRIVING LICENCES FROM 1998.

text.p: The government planned to crack down on false driving licences being issued by corrupt officials, Transport Minister Mac Maharaj said on Wednesday.
In a mini-debate in parliament, Maharaj said drivers would have to apply for new licences which will be issued in a new credit card format from March 1, 1998.
Maharaj said driving licence codes would also be changed to conform with of the Southern African Development Community grouping.

"Licence authorisation will be administered and controlled through the NaTIS computer system, which will record the details both of the testing official involved and the centre where the test was conducted."
He said the licence card would have special features such as a water mark and security printing to discourage fraud.
A photograph, signature and fingerprint of the holder and a two-dimensional barcode will also be featured.
From 1998 driving offences will earn drivers penalty points and face suspension of licences.
